status_summary: The National Park Service proposed on 2026-03-10 (91 FR 11483) to restore its pre-2015 regulations for hunting, fishing and trapping in Alaska national preserves; comments closed 2026-04-24 after an extension. A final rule, Alaska; Wildlife, Harvest, and Access (91 FR 65985, doc 2026-21299), was filed for public inspection on 2026-10-16 and is dated for publication on 2026-10-19 with an effective date of 2026-11-18; it rescinds the 2015 changes not already reversed in 2020, most of the 2017 rule and the 2024 rule in full, and allows bear harvest over bait under state law. The rule covers National Park Service areas only, states that the agency does not defer to the State while state law governs harvest to the extent federal law permits, and says regulated harvest cannot operate as predator control. No new Fish and Wildlife Service rule or state memorandum of understanding was found; the proposal notes that Congress nullified the Service's 2016 refuge rule in 2017 (Public Law 115-20).

timeline.event: The National Park Service proposes to restore pre-2015 hunting and trapping rules in Alaska national preserves and rescind its 2015, 2017 and 2024 rules, including the bear-baiting prohibition (91 FR 11483; comments due 2026-04-09).
The National Park Service extends the comment period on the proposal by 15 days, to 2026-04-24, after multiple requests for more time.

The National Park Service filed for public inspection the final rule Alaska; Wildlife, Harvest, and Access (91 FR 65985, doc 2026-21299), scheduled for Federal Register publication on 2026-10-19; it restores the pre-2015 harvest and closure framework in Alaska national preserves, rescinds the 2015, 2017 (except two definitions) and 2024 changes including the bear-baiting limits, and takes effect on 2026-11-18.

title: Revoke federal Alaska predator control and bear baiting limits; defer to state management
uncertainties: The final rule was read on federalregister.gov through its first 100,000 of 129,146 characters, covering the summary, the rescission provisions, the bear-baiting change and the comment discussion; the signature block and the remaining tail were not read. The rule received 5,172 comments, with organizations representing more than 48,000 signatories; the figure of 53,801 shown earlier on the proposed-rule page was a different count. The rule states that it does not defer to the State and that regulated harvest cannot act as predator control, so it only partly matches the Mandate's framing. The state memoranda of understanding and any Alaska-specific Fish and Wildlife Service action were checked only through Federal Register queries. Congressional Review Act activity on the 2024 rule was not checked.
